title: Overdubbing a Moog string part with Jimmy Smith
summary: Jones set up a Moog and showed Jimmy Smith how to play the string part rather than writing it.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: You told me that in between interviews here (Inaudible), you overdubbed some music with Jimmy Smith the organ player...
And you said he had called you and asked
you about some music for moog, right? \ (Inaudible). Moog synthesizer.
And that was the first time you had ever done that. And you not only wrote it but you played it, right?

No, let me put it this way. I didn't write it. You see, because what I did, I took the moog home and set the stops to the string -- he just wanted a string sound, you know? And then I went back with him in the studio and you know how Jimmy plays -- he's beautiful the way he plays, but overdubbed this -- this is where that writing and simplicity, that discipline comes in. So I would go out and play and I would show him what I wanted him to do. And he did it beautifully. I'd go in the booth with his wife, who is a very brilliant woman, you know? And -- yeah, she's very -- she's got her head together. And then I could listen to it, and he did, he caught on. And it was better that he did it, because you needed an organ touch for that, and I had studied organ, you know, but I hadn't played it in years, you know. But he plays it all the time, so you have to have that kind of organ touch, you know, to hold that together, but I would show him as though I had written an arrangement, you know, what to play. And it jelled in with what we already had on the tape. It jelled in very well. And they were quite happy about it. The sides turned out good, you know?
